title: Foundation — Dumbbells Intermediate
subtitle: General base building with light load
coaching_note: This sits under whatever sport you're building toward — the point is a strong, balanced base, not chasing heavy numbers. Pick a dumbbell weight you can control for every rep of every set. If your form breaks down on the last few reps, that's the right weight — not too light.

exercises.name: Jumping Jacks
exercises.form_cue: Full range — arms overhead, feet wide. Land soft.
exercises.why: Gets the whole body warm fast before you pick up weight.

exercises.name: Bodyweight Reverse Lunge
exercises.form_cue: Step back, drop the back knee toward the floor, front shin stays vertical.
exercises.why: Rehearses the lunge pattern and opens the hip flexors before loading.

phases.name: Lower Body
phases.coaching_note: Start light. You should be able to nail the last rep of set one with the same form as the first.

exercises.name: Goblet Squat
exercises.form_cue: Hold one dumbbell at chest height with both hands. Chest tall, sit back and down, knees track your toes.
exercises.why: The goblet position keeps your torso upright, which is far more forgiving on the lower back than a barbell squat while you build the pattern.

exercises.name: Dumbbell Romanian Deadlift
exercises.form_cue: Soft knees, push your hips straight back, dumbbells stay close to your legs. Stop when you feel the hamstring stretch — that's your range, not the floor.
exercises.why: Builds the posterior chain that keeps you upright and powerful in almost every sport movement.

exercises.name: Reverse Lunge (dumbbells)
exercises.form_cue: Dumbbells at your sides, step back into the lunge, front knee stays over the ankle, not past the toes.
exercises.why: Single-leg strength closes gaps between your stronger and weaker side that a bilateral squat can hide.

exercises.name: Dumbbell Row
exercises.form_cue: Flat back, brace on a bench with one hand. Pull the dumbbell to your hip, elbow close to your body, squeeze at the top.
exercises.why: Pulling strength balances all the pressing in daily life and most sport-specific work — keeps shoulders healthy long-term.

exercises.name: Dumbbell Shoulder Press
exercises.form_cue: Start at shoulder height, press straight overhead without arching your lower back. Ribs stay down.
exercises.why: Overhead strength and stability — most sports ask your shoulders to work overhead at some point.

exercises.name: Dumbbell Bicep Curl
exercises.form_cue: Elbows pinned at your sides, no swinging. Full range, control the lowering.
exercises.why: Small accessory work — keeps the elbow and forearm resilient under the bigger lifts.

exercises.name: Plank
exercises.form_cue: Forearms down, straight line from head to heel. No sagging hips, no raised butt.
exercises.why: Anterior core endurance — the foundation everything else sits on top of.

exercises.name: Standing Hip Flexor Stretch
exercises.form_cue: Step into a lunge, tuck your tailbone under, gently drive the hips forward.
exercises.why: Lunges and squats tighten the hip flexors — stretch them before you leave the mat.

progression_notes: Add 1-2kg per dumbbell once all sets hit the top of the rep range with clean form for two sessions in a row. Add a third lunge set before adding weight to the lunge.
